title: ServiceTitan Voice Agent vs Podium Larry
seo_title: ServiceTitan Voice Agent vs Podium Larry: Pricing & Business Fit
description: ServiceTitan Voice Agent vs Podium Larry: compare native booking, dispatch fees, bundled software and costs, plus Off The Clock’s job quotes.
intro: ServiceTitan automates calls within its account. Podium packages Larry with an operating system. Off The Clock gives you a separate operator built around the customer’s job price.
verdict: Choose Off The Clock when the purchase is about answering, pricing and booking the job—not replacing your field-service platform. QuoteDone extends your rates to both calls and website inquiries.

sections: Native account context is real—but it is not a job quote

ServiceTitan’s controls tie the agent to job types, follow-up questions and dispatch-fee messages. Podium describes access to its dispatch board, price book, technician availability and customer history. Neither product should be portrayed as a disconnected message pad. [[st-settings]] [[podium-larry]]

The remaining question is what the price represents. A configured attendance fee can answer “what does the visit cost?” without answering “what does this project cost?” Those are different amounts, not different labels for the same feature.
QuoteDone makes the project the unit of the conversation

A roof-repair request can depend on the confirmed repair details and measured affected area. QuoteDone combines supported inputs with the owner’s rates instead of promoting a trip fee into an entire job price.

The operator answers questions, books, transfers and follows up around that calculation. Website visitors can start through the QuoteDone widget. If diagnosis or measurements are still needed, the complete request comes to the owner with the collected details and no unsupported total.

That is Off The Clock’s reason to be here: a complete operator with owner-controlled quoting. It does not require a new technician-management platform, and a native ServiceTitan connector is not part of this comparison.

ServiceTitan’s indexed public Voice Agent offer is $2.75 per call with a 12-month rate lock and monthly usage billing. The direct page is JavaScript-rendered; the source register records the indexed retrieval. Podium’s home-services plan requires a sales quote. [[st-pricing]] [[podium-plans]]

QuoteDone is $279 per month with 1,200 minutes, the operator and website quote widget. Extra usage is $0.35 per minute; there is no setup fee. The per-call and per-minute offers require actual call-duration data to compare usage costs.
Separate business rules from software replacement

ServiceTitan documents multiple agents with independent greetings, job types, fees and number assignments. Podium’s advertised bundle includes the wider dispatch, technician and payment system. Those are different forms of operational scope. [[st-multi]] [[podium-plans]]

Off The Clock keeps its focus on incoming customers and the owner’s pricing. You retain decisions about rates, included scope and which exceptions require you. The aim is to remove repetitive quote conversations, not ownership of the quote.
decision: Choose Off The Clock when your customer needs the job price—not merely the visit fee—and you want the operator to handle that next step. QuoteDone gives your rates a role in the inquiry without making a platform migration the price of admission.
card_description: A native per-call agent versus Larry’s bundled platform. Distinguish dispatch-fee answers from QuoteDone’s owner-priced project calculation.
